claim: Tamina Therme 2026 weekday day ticket (bath only) is CHF 67, weekend CHF 74; bath + sauna day ticket CHF 85 weekday / CHF 92 weekend.
quote: Day Ticket Prices for Bath Only: CHF 67.00 Monday-Friday and CHF 74.00 on weekends/public holidays. Day Ticket Prices for Bath & Sauna: CHF 85.00 Monday-Friday and CHF 92.00 on weekends/public holidays.

claim: Tamina Therme spans over 8,600 m² and features indoor/outdoor pools, water-jet baths, Nordic kelo sauna houses, and a setting of oak woodwork and natural light; Grand Resort hotel guests get free admission.
quote: The Tamina Therme is described as 'an architectural masterpiece' that 'unites traditional spa culture with innovation and modern style – over 8,600 square metres.' ... 'a huge variety of indoor and outdoor pools and various warm and cold water baths with water jet and shower features.' Hotel guests receive free admission during their stay.

claim: The Tamina Therme bath complex has six indoor/outdoor pools with current channels, neck showers and underwater massage, plus a coed sauna world (16+) including steam room, Nero, Kelo with infusion ceremonies, and a Latvian Pirts.
quote: six indoor and outdoor pools ... float in the current channel, enjoy a neck shower or an underwater massage ... a temple made of wood, marble and gold ... steam room, Nero sauna, Kelo sauna with infusion ceremonies, and a Latvian Pirts sauna featuring body scrubs.

claim: Benedictine monks discovered the 36.5°C Tamina spring in 1242; early bathers were lowered 70 metres into the gorge in baskets, and Paracelsus wrote about the healing waters in the 16th century.
quote: discovered by Benedictine monks in 1242. Initially, accessing the gorge was perilous—early guests were 'lowered down 70 metres in baskets.' After physician Paracelsus wrote about its healing properties in the 16th century, pilgrims flocked to Tamina.

claim: The Tamina Gorge / Old Bath Pfäfers 2026 season runs 2 May–25 October, with daily hours 10:00–17:15 (May–Aug) and 10:00–16:15 (late Aug–Oct); admission to the gorge is a flat CHF 5 for all ages.
quote: Season: May 2, 2026 – October 25, 2026. May 2 - August 30: daily from 10:00 a.m. to 5:15 p.m. August 31 - October 25: daily from 10:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Admission to the Tamina Gorge costs CHF 5.00 per person.

claim: PostBus line 453 (Schluchtenbus) reaches Old Bath Pfäfers from Bad Ragaz station in ~15 minutes; adult fare CHF 6 one-way / CHF 11 return, children/dog CHF 4 / CHF 6.
quote: Children 4–16 years old / dog: one-way journey CHF 4.00 / return journey CHF 6.00. Adults: one-way journey CHF 6.00 / return journey CHF 11.00 ... From May to October between 10.30 a.m. and 5 p.m ... mid-May to August between 9.30 a.m. and 6 p.m

claim: The Tamina Gorge is 750 m long and 70 m deep; visitors walk a 450 m secured path to a spring grotto where the 36.5°C Tamina spring gushes out at 8,000 litres per minute.
quote: The crevice, which the river dug into the rock, is 750 m long and 70 m deep. The gorge can be walked on a 450 m long secured path ... The 36.5 °C warm Tamina spring gushes out of the rock here with an impressive 8000 liters of water per min.

claim: The Old Bath Pfäfers is Switzerland's oldest preserved Baroque bath (built 1704–1718, renovated 1983–1995), with a bath-and-monastery museum, a Paracelsus memorial, a neo-Gothic bathing chapel and an on-site restaurant.
quote: Switzerland's oldest baroque bathing facility was built between 1704 and 1718 and gently renovated between 1983 and 1995 ... a bathing and monastery museum with a Paracelsus memorial, a neo-Gothic bathing chapel, and a restaurant.

claim: The Pizol 5-lake hike covers 11.4 km with ~553 m ascent / ~911 m descent, takes 4.5 hours, is rated medium difficulty, and requires hikers to reach Gaffia chairlift by 16:30 or Pizolhütte by 16:00 to catch the last descent (Furt gondola 17:30).
quote: 11.4 km | Duration: 4.30 h | Elevation gain: 553m 911m ... Hikers must reach the Gaffia chairlift by 4:30 PM or Pizolhütte by 4:00 PM. The final gondola descent from Furt departs at 5:30 PM.

claim: Pizol's hiking and sightseeing season starts Ascension Day 14 May 2026 with daily Bad Ragaz gondola operation; all five summer lifts open daily from Saturday 27 June through Saturday 18 October 2026.
quote: The hiking and sightseeing season will kick off on Ascension Day, May 14, 2026, with the start of daily operations on the Bad Ragaz gondola. Starting Saturday, June 27, all five summer lifts at Pizol will open and operate daily through Saturday, October 18, 2026.

claim: The full 5-lake route is realistically accessible only from mid-July to mid-October because of lingering snow on the high traverse; even in July snowfields and névés often remain on the path.
quote: The hike will be accessible from mid-July to mid-October ... even in July during a heat wave, there was still snow on the path and several névés (snow patches) to cross.

claim: The Heidiweg is a 6.5 km easy circular walk from Maienfeld station through vineyards to Heididorf, Heidihof viewpoint and Heidi's fountain, taking about 1 h 30 min and marked with red 'Heidiweg' signs.
quote: Maienfeld station to Heididorf: approximately 40 minutes; Complete Heidiweg loop: approximately 1 hour 30 minutes; Total distance: 6.5 km ... signalized with red directional signs marked 'Heidiweg'

claim: A longer Heidi Adventure Trail continues from Heididorf up to Heidi-Alp on the Ochsenberg, climbing roughly 450 m with twelve themed stations and taking about 1 h 45 min one-way.
quote: the Heidi Adventure Trail to Heidialp takes around an hour and three quarters ... if you don't feel like hiking the 450 metres up to the Heidialp, you can follow the trail over fields and meadows to Hotel Restaurant Heidihof.

claim: Flumserberg cable cars (SeeJet sections 1-2, BergJet, Chrüz, Prodalp-Express, Prodkamm) close briefly 26-29 May 2026 for the seasonal switch, then resume partial operation the following weekend ahead of full summer service.
quote: All facilities, including GB SeeJet, will be closed from Tuesday, May 26 to Friday, May 29, 2026. Partial operations will resume next weekend.

claim: Flumserberg opens partial summer operations over Whitsun weekend 23-25 May 2026 with tobogganing, climbing, biking and hiking up to ~1500 m, then commences daily operation including BergJet on 6 June 2026.
quote: The summer season will begin with partial operations over the Whitsun weekend (23–25 May 2026) ... Daily operation, including the BergJet gondola, will commence on June 6, 2026.

claim: The Walensee north-shore hike from Weesen via Betlis and the Seerenbachfälle waterfalls to car-free Quinten is a moderate ~3.5-4 hour route with ~500 m elevation gain along forested cliff paths.
quote: The Weesen - Quinten via Lake Walen is considered a moderate route with an elevation gain of 1,633 ft, taking approximately 3.5–4 hr to complete.

claim: Quinten is reachable only on foot or by Walensee ferry and is known for its Mediterranean microclimate with terraced vineyards and fig trees, making the shore hike viable already in late spring.
quote: Quinten Village is accessible only by foot or boat, this secluded lakeside hamlet is renowned for its Mediterranean microclimate, terraced vineyards, and fig trees

claim: The Falknis (2,562 m) on the Swiss-Liechtenstein border above Maienfeld is a demanding T4-level alpine hike requiring sure-footedness, taking 5-7 hours and rewarding climbers with views as far as Lake Constance.
quote: Falknis is on the border between Liechtenstein and Switzerland ... lies at 2,560 m above sea level. The view from Falknis extends northward beyond Lake Constance ... For the downhill variant you can calculate 5 to 6 hours, if you want to hike uphill the other way around, you should calculate 7 hours.

claim: The Alvier summit (2,343 m) above Sevelen offers a 360° panorama across Walensee, the Rhine valley and Lake Constance via an exposed rocky trail from Windegg through Alp Arin requiring sure-footedness.
quote: summit at 2,342 meters offers a 360-degree panorama over Lake Walen, the Rhine Valley, and all the way to Lake Constance ... starts in Windegg and then over the Alp Arin at 1518m and then up to the Alvier mountain peak at 2343m.

claim: Vaduz Castle is the private residence of the Princely Family and its interior is closed to the public, but the grounds are accessible via a 15-minute uphill footpath behind the Landesmuseum, opened to visitors only on August 15 (National Day).
quote: Vaduz Castle - Official tourism website of the Principality of Liechtenstein. The castle serves as the private residence of the Princely Family of Liechtenstein and the interior is not open to the public.

claim: The Liechtensteinisches Landesmuseum (Städtle 43, Vaduz) opens Tue-Sun 10am-5pm (Wed to 8pm), CHF 10 adult, with a combo ticket including the Treasure Chamber for CHF 13.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday 10 am to 5 pm. Wednesday 10 am to 8 pm. Combo ticket covers both the National Museum and Treasure Chamber. Regular CHF 13.

claim: The Schatzkammer (Treasure Chamber) is open daily 10am-5pm and holds princely treasures from five centuries including Fabergé eggs (Apple Blossom Egg), Apollo 11/17 moon rocks, a replica of the Princely Hat, and a perpetual calendar made for Emperor Rudolf II.
quote: Open daily, 10 am to 5 pm. Treasures from five centuries that is unique in the Alpine region. Fabergé eggs and moon rocks from the Apollo 11 (1969) and Apollo 17 (1972) manned lunar missions.

claim: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein (Städtle 32, Vaduz) is closed Mondays, open Tue-Sun 10am-5pm (Thu to 8pm), CHF 12-15 adult, with free admission every Wednesday and August 15.
quote: Closed on Mondays, open Tuesday-Wednesday from 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Thursday from 10:00 AM - 8:00 PM. Entry fees are CHF 12-15 for adults. Every Wednesday and on August 15th admission is free.

claim: The Hofkellerei des Fürsten von Liechtenstein in Vaduz runs public tastings Mon-Sat at 15:00 including a champagne reception, vineyard/cellar tour and six wines (~60-90 minutes); groups under 6 need no booking, larger groups must email office@hofkellerei.li.
quote: The tasting includes a champagne reception, a guided tour of the vineyard and cellar and a tasting of six selected wines. It takes place from Monday to Saturday at 15:00, and the event lasts around 60 to 90 minutes.

claim: The Princely Winery's Herawingert vineyard in Vaduz spans four hectares with southwest exposure and a mild foehn climate, considered one of the best vineyards in the Rhine Valley.
quote: With its four hectares of vineyards, Herawingert is one of the best vineyards in the Rhine Valley due to its south-western exposure and mild foehn climate.

claim: The Liechtenstein Center tourist office (Städtle 39, Vaduz) sells the novelty souvenir passport stamp for CHF 3 / EUR 3.30 and is open seven days a week.
quote: Souvenir stamp: CHF 3 / EUR 3.30 (complimentary for ALL INCLUSIVE Adventure Pass holders). Expert information available seven days a week.

claim: The Liechtenstein-Weg (Liechtenstein Trail) is a 75 km route through all 11 municipalities, divided into five official stages, accompanied by the LIstory app delivering cultural/historical commentary, with luggage transport bookable.
quote: 75 km of exciting stories, sights and magnificent views. The LIstory app accompanies visitors with exciting stories and insights into the country's culture and history.

claim: The Fürstensteig is a 5.9 km circular alpine hike (~2h45, 478 m ascent, max 1929 m) starting at Alp Gaflei, with exposed sections secured by wire ropes; surefootedness and a head for heights required; reach the trailhead via Liechtenstein Bus to Gaflei, Kurhaus.
quote: Distance: 5.9 km. Duration: 2 hours 45 minutes. Elevation Gain/Loss: 478m ascent, 481m descent. The Fürstensteig requires surefootedness and a head for heights. Exposed sections secured with wire ropes.

claim: The Liechtensteinisches PostMuseum in the Englanderbau, Vaduz, is open daily 10am-5pm with free admission, showing every stamp issued since 1912.
quote: Postmuseum Vaduz, established in 1936, is dedicated to the history of Liechtenstein's postal service and philately. Located in the Englanderbau in Vaduz. Free admission. Daily 10 am to 5 pm.

claim: From Bad Ragaz to Vaduz is roughly 13 miles; train to Schaan-Vaduz via Sargans runs hourly in ~16 minutes, while LIEmobil bus 11 from Sargans Bahnhof to Vaduz Post departs every 30 minutes (~32 min), and driving takes about 13 minutes.
quote: The distance between Bad Ragaz and Vaduz is 13 miles. Verkehrsbetrieb Liechtensteinmobil operates a bus from Sargans, Bahnhof to Vaduz, Post every 30 minutes, and the journey takes 32 min.

claim: LIEmobil operates the Liechtenstein public bus network; line 11 is the main Sargans Bahnhof - Vaduz - Schaan - Buchs/Feldkirch backbone, integrated with Swiss rail tickets and the Swiss Travel Pass.
quote: Timetable, Operation notices, News. LIEmobil 11 bus Route Map - Sargans Bahnhof.

claim: The Liechtenstein Trail's five stages run 8.5-19.6 km per day; stage 2 from Triesenberg passes Schalun Castle ruins and Vaduz Castle, and stage 3 leaves Vaduz past the Court Winery and Roman ruins to Schaan.
quote: Following the official five stages will see you walking a minimum of 8.5 and maximum of 19.6 kilometres per day. Stage 2 leads from Triesenberg via the historic Prufatscheng farmstead past the majestic Vaduz Castle.

claim: Heididorf 2026 adult ticket CHF 14.90, child (5-14) CHF 6.90, under-4 free, group rate CHF 12.50 for 10+ adults.
quote: Adult Ticket (Single): CHF 14.90; Child Ticket: CHF 6.90 (applies to ages 5-14; children under 4 are free); Group Rate (10+ adults): CHF 12.50.

claim: Heididorf 2026 season runs 13 March – 1 November, daily 10:00–17:00, last entry 15:45.
quote: The Heididorf (Heidi's Village) is from the 13. March until 1. November 2026 daily open from 10am to 5pm.

claim: The Heididorf is built around a 300-year-old original Heidi-Haus, plus alp cottage replica, school in the town hall, goat barn, Spyri exhibit and Switzerland's smallest post office.
quote: The 300 year old Heidi's House is the origin of the world famous story of Heidi. Johanna Spyri was inspired by the people and ways of life living here for her story of Heidi.

claim: The PostBus 'Heidibus' runs Maienfeld station ↔ Heididorf on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays from end-April to mid-October, avoiding the steep uphill walk.
quote: The Heidibus operates on Saturdays, Sundays and general public holidays from the end of April to mid-October... connects Maienfeld railway station to Heididorf, eliminating a steep 40-minute hike uphill.

claim: Heidialp Ochsenberg (the 'real' grandfather's hut on the alp) is reached on foot in ~1h15 from Martin's Fountain car park or ~1h40 from Heididorf via the 12-station Heidi adventure trail; food and drink served at the alp.
quote: From Heidi Village (Oberrofels): walking time approx. 1h 40 min along a narrow trail connecting to a natural street featuring 12 educational stations... At the top you will find a team of huts with food and drink and pure nature to linger.

claim: Heidialp sits at 1,111 m and the Heidi Erlebnisweg from Heididorf up to the alp takes about 1h45 with 12 themed stations bringing the story to life.
quote: Vom Heididorf auf die Heidialp (Ochsenberg) 1111 m.ü.M. ... The varied and more challenging Heidi Adventure Trail to Heidialp (Ochsenberg) takes around an hour and three quarters.

claim: Maienfeld sits in the Bündner Herrschaft wine region (Maienfeld, Jenins, Malans, Fläsch), Switzerland's premier Pinot Noir area and the landscape that inspired Spyri.
quote: The Bündner Herrschaft is 'the small region of great wines.' ... renowned for producing award-winning Pinot Noir, with the Pinot Noir world championship title has gone to the Bündner Herrschaft region several times.

claim: Johanna Spyri was inspired by the Bündner Herrschaft over 120 years ago and the original Heidi village in Maienfeld now draws ~150,000 visitors a year.
quote: The author, Johanna Spyri, was inspired by the scenic Bündner Herrschaft 120 years ago to write the famous bestseller. The original Heidi village attracts around 150,000 visitors to Maienfeld every year.

claim: TripAdvisor reviews split between fans calling it 'magical' and critics flagging steep walks, animal-welfare concerns and commercialisation.
quote: Beautiful place for all ages... very relaxed... They have no accommodations for elderly visitors... expected to walk up steep long hills... goats didn't look particularly healthy.

claim: Blogger verdict: not a Disneyland — 'aiming to be as authentic as possible' while handling 150k visitors; ~10 min drive from the Grand Hotel Quellenhof in Bad Ragaz.
quote: aiming to be as authentic as possible while managing the roughly 150'000 visitors per year... less than a 10 minute drive from the Grand Hotel Quellenhof.

claim: Independent blog take: experience is modest in scale, 2–3 hours max, works best as a literary nostalgia stop rather than a standalone destination; the walk through vineyards is the real attraction.
quote: The walk up to Heididorf through the vineyards is worth the effort because you get some picturesque views of the mountains... most activities take 2-3 hours maximum.

claim: The 'Heidi Express' is actually the Landquart→Klosters/Davos→Tirano scenic train (~5h, May 28–Oct 15 season), not a shuttle inside Maienfeld.
quote: The Heidi Express runs from Landquart in northeastern Switzerland through stunning mountain scenery and the resorts of Klosters and Davos down to the palm trees of Tirano in northern Italy. The trip takes nearly five hours and is only available May 28 to Oct. 15.

claim: Pinot Noir (Blauburgunder) accounts for 68% of Graubünden plantings on ~287 ha of roughly 400 ha total; Bündner Herrschaft comprises Fläsch, Maienfeld, Jenins and Malans and produces more than 50 wines from 45 grape varieties under Föhn-driven warmth.
quote: Pinot Noir (Blauburgunder) comprises 68% of vineyard plantings, covering 287 hectares of the region's ~400-hectare total. ... The Föhn winds—locally called 'grape cookers'—create the warmest conditions in German-speaking Switzerland.

claim: The Föhn ('traubenkocher' or grape cooker) is the warm dry Alpine wind that ripens Pinot Noir in Bündner Herrschaft; a 2014 late-season foehn lifted Pinot Noir Brix from 20.8° to 23.5°, and the wind also suppresses mold and mildew.
quote: During the 2014 harvest, a late-season foehn increased Pinot Noir Brix levels by approximately 15%, from 20.8° to 23.5°. ... The foehn is, therefore, a powerfully 'antiseptic' wind that discourages the growth of mold and mildew.

claim: Iconic Fläsch producer Gantenbein (founded 1982 by Martha and Daniel Gantenbein) explicitly does not offer tours or tastings, citing demand vs. small-team capacity, and is not accepting new customers.
quote: We have a large number of requests for visits and tastings; unfortunately we are not able to offer tours with our small dedicated team. ... we are sold out every year. Therefore, we not able to take new customers for years

claim: Domaine Donatsch in Malans (5 generations, founded 1897) opens its Winzerstube zum Ochsen Wed–Sun with tours by appointment; their Pinot Noirs tier as 'Tradition' (village), 'Passion' (premier-cru style, 30% new oak) and 'Unique' (grand-cru style, new Burgundy barrels) — Martin Donatsch won World Champion Pinot Noir Producer at the 2011 Mondial du Pinot Noir.
quote: The wine tavern is open Wednesday-Sunday with tours by appointment. ... Martin was named 'WORLD CHAMPION PINOT NOIR PRODUCER' at the Mondial du Pinot Noir 2011 for the second time in succession.

claim: Schloss Salenegg in Maienfeld — claiming roots to 1068 as one of Europe's oldest wineries — welcomes walk-in tastings without appointment and runs guided cellar tours every Friday at 3 pm and the first Saturday of the month at 2 pm, with traditional Pinot Noir alongside Chardonnay and PIWI whites.
quote: Weingut Schloss Salenegg is free to visit and taste the wines without an appointment, and they also offer cellar tours every Friday at 3 pm and the first Saturday of the month at 2 pm.

claim: The Swiss Fine Wine Trail through Bündner Herrschaft is a 7.3 km easy walk (~2 h, 138 m ascent) from Malans station via Jenins to Maienfeld station, with multiple cellar stops for Pinot Noir tasting along the way.
quote: 7.3 km long ... 2 hours 4 minutes to complete ... Starting from Malans train station, the route passes through Jenins and Maienfeld, ending at Maienfeld's railway station. ... 'The walk is easy and they are many stops along the trail to taste the local wines including their world famous Pinot Noir.'

claim: Alter Torkel in Jenins (Jeninserstrasse 3) runs a 'Fine-Wineing' concept — wine determines the dish — with 21 open Graubünden wines and the self-styled largest Graubünden wine archive (>1,500 references); kitchen open lunch and dinner Mon–Sat plus Sunday lunch only.
quote: 'Der Wein bestimmt das Gericht' (The wine determines the dish). The restaurant features 21 wines available by the glass from Graubünden and operates what it claims is 'the world's largest wine archive of Graubünden vintners.'

claim: Alter Torkel is rated 14 Gault Millau points and since 2020 is run by Julia and Oliver Friedrich with chef David Esser, sommelier Jennifer List leading the wine program built around producers like Gantenbein, Donatsch, Obrecht and Adank.
quote: Alter Torkel ... is listed with 14 points in the Gault Millau guide ... Since 2020, it has been run by Julia and Oliver Friedrich ... kitchen is led by chef David Esser, with a wine team including sommelier Jennifer List

claim: Decanter frames Bündner Herrschaft as the 'Burgundy of Switzerland', with nearly 80% red-grape plantings dominated by Pinot Noir; the Föhn ('traubenkocher') funnels warm dry air through the San Bernardino corridor to clear skies and accelerate ripening.
quote: Almost 80% of the vineyard area is planted with red grape varieties, of which Pinot Noir is the undisputed star. ... Known locally as traubenkocher, or 'grape cooker', it funnels warm, dry air down from the Alps, clearing the skies and accelerating ripening.

claim: Weingut Obrecht in Jenins (Francisca and Christian Obrecht, 5th generation, 7 ha, Demeter-certified biodynamic since 2017) is a leading Bündner Herrschaft producer and offers a self-service bottle dispenser on site for visiting tasters.
quote: Francisca and Christian Obrecht in Jenins are leading producers of the Bündner Herrschaft, managing the winery in its fifth generation across seven hectares following biodynamic guidelines (Demeter certified since 2017) ... their on-site bottle dispenser allows for an efficient snapshot of their craft.

claim: Graubünden Tourism's 'Backpack wine tasting' self-guided package through the Bündner Herrschaft vineyards starts from CHF 75 per person.
quote: Backpack wine tasting in the Bündner Herrschaft starts from CHF 75

claim: Between April and November, Maienfeld vintners take turns hosting weekend open-cellar tastings in their Torkels with local specialties; the bus line Bad Ragaz–Fläsch–Maienfeld–Jenins–Malans–Landquart connects the wine villages directly to Bad Ragaz.
quote: Between April and November, the Maienfelder vintners take it in turns to offer invitations to weekend wine tastings in their cellars or «Torkels». Local specialties are served with the wine. ... Bus line: Bad Ragaz-Fläsch-Maienfeld-Jenins-Malans-Landquart

claim: Chur claims to be Switzerland's oldest city with a 13,000-year settlement history, and its traffic-free old town is one of the best-preserved medieval centres in the country.
quote: Switzerland's oldest city, with more than a 13,000-year-long history of settlement. The old town itself is regarded as one of the country's best-preserved medieval centers.

claim: Chur's car-free old town features the picturesque Arcas square with painted façades and outdoor cafés, plus a Saturday farmers' market and monthly flea market on the Arcas.
quote: The most atmospheric is the Arcas, a small square surrounded by painted façades and outdoor café tables... the monthly flea market on Arcas square

claim: The Bündner Kunstmuseum sits on Postplatz in central Chur, a 5-minute walk from the train and coach station, and after its 2014–2016 expansion has become one of Switzerland's most attractive public museums.
quote: situated in the centre of Chur on the 'Postplatz' square, with a 5 minute walk from both the train and coach station. With the expansion (2014-2016), the Graubünden Art Museum has become one of the most attractive museums in Switzerland

claim: The Rätisches Museum in Chur occupies a Baroque patrician house from 1675 and displays archaeological, cultural and folk-art objects covering Graubünden from prehistory to the present.
quote: The Rätische Museum, housed in a baroque patrician house built in 1675, illustrates Graubünden history, with a permanent exhibition that includes archaeological, cultural and folk art objects from throughout Canton Graubünden from prehistoric times to the present.

claim: Chur is only about 25 minutes from Bad Ragaz by train or car.
quote: Chur is only 25 minutes from Bad Ragaz by train or car.

claim: Werdenberg Castle, the historical seat of the Counts of Werdenberg, is roughly 800 years old; today the site contains two museums (the castle museum and the Schlangenhaus Museum in the town), open seasonally 1 April–31 October.
quote: Two interconnected museums operate seasonally (April 1–October 31). The castle museum presents three historical periods on separate floors, while the Schlangenhaus Museum in the town below offers exhibits from settlement origins to present day

claim: Werdenberg is described as the smallest 'town' in Switzerland, with intact medieval timber-frame houses below its castle, founded around 1230 by Count Rudolf I of Montfort.
quote: Werdenberg is the smallest city in Switzerland... The castle from the late Middle Ages with the tower, palace, additions and courtyard was founded around 1230 by Count Rudolf I of Montfort.

claim: Sargans Castle was built or expanded in the 12th century (Hugo built/expanded it before his death in 1228); since 1899 the local heritage association has run it and it now houses the Sarganserland Museum, a Swiss heritage site of national significance.
quote: Hugo...built or expanded Sargans Castle before his death in 1228... Since 1899, it has been run by the local church and now houses the Sarganserland museum... a Swiss heritage site of national significance

claim: The Sarganserland Museum at Sargans Castle is one of Switzerland's oldest regional museums (established 1904), spread over six floors of the tower; it was named Museum of the Year in Europe in 1983 and is open Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00, April to October.
quote: one of Switzerland's oldest, established in 1904. The Sarganserland Museum is housed in the tower of Sargans Castle, spread over six floors... The castle won the "Museum of the Year in Europe" in 1983... open from April to October, Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00

claim: Pfäfers Abbey was founded in 731 from Reichenau as Monasterium Fabariense; after a 1665 fire it was rebuilt in Baroque style and the new abbey church was dedicated in 1694.
quote: the abbey was established in 731, founded from Reichenau Abbey as "Monasterium Fabariense"... Following a devastating fire in 1665 that destroyed the medieval structures, the monastery was rebuilt in Baroque style... The 'new abbey church' was dedicated in 1694

claim: Altes Bad Pfäfers, below the Pfäfers village, is described as the oldest Baroque spa facility in Switzerland and houses both a bath museum and a monastery museum, with a Paracelsus memorial site and neo-Gothic bath chapel.
quote: the oldest Baroque spa facility in Switzerland... functions as both a bath and monastery museum, featuring a 'Paracelsus memorial site' and a 'neo-Gothic bath chapel'

claim: 2026 is not a Bad RagARTz exhibition year; the 10th Swiss Triennial of Sculpture runs 1 May–31 October 2027 in Bad Ragaz (with Vaduz), with applications open until 31 July 2026.
quote: The upcoming triennial exhibition is scheduled for May 1 – October 31, 2027. This will be the 10th edition of the Swiss Triennial of Sculpture.

claim: Each edition of the Bad RagARTz open-air sculpture exhibition draws up to nearly one million visitors and places around 400 sculptures across the spa-town parks of Bad Ragaz and urban Vaduz, with a Festival of Small Sculptures held at Altes Bad Pfäfers in the Tamina gorge.
quote: Each edition of the exhibition attracts up to nearly one million visitors, with around 400 sculptures transforming Bad Ragaz into a vibrant city of shapes and colours... Festival of Small Sculptures in Altes Bad Pfäfers in the Taminaschlucht gorge
